question.:question/problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a = ⟨k, 1, 1⟩$, $b = ⟨5, 0, 4⟩$, and $c = ⟨6, 2, 5⟩$ are coplanar.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot(b\times c)&=|\begin{aligned}k & 1 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 4 \\ 6 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}|\\ &=((k)\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}|)+((-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}|)+((1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}|)\\ &=((k)\cdot ((0)\cdot (5)-(4)\cdot (2)))+((-1)\cdot ((5)\cdot (5)-(4)\cdot (6)))+((1)\cdot ((5)\cdot (2)-(0)\cdot (6)))\\ &=((k)\cdot (-8))+((-1)\cdot (1))+((1)\cdot (10))\\ &=(-8k)+(-1)+(10)\\ &=9-8k\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}9-8k&=0\\ -8k&=-9\\ k&=\frac{9}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=\frac{9}{8}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 3(11-k) & =0 \\ 11-k & =0 \\ k & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=11.$

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot(b\times c)&=|\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & 7 \\ 7 & k & -4 \\ 5 & 5 & 8\end{aligned}|\\ &=((6)\cdot |\begin{aligned}k & -4 \\ 5 & 8\end{aligned}|)+((-5)\cdot |\begin{aligned}7 & -4 \\ 5 & 8\end{aligned}|)+((7)\cdot |\begin{aligned}7 & k \\ 5 & 5\end{aligned}|)\\ &=((6)\cdot ((k)\cdot (8)-(-4)\cdot (5)))+((-5)\cdot ((7)\cdot (8)-(-4)\cdot (5)))+((7)\cdot ((7)\cdot (5)-(k)\cdot (5)))\\ &=((6)\cdot (8k+20))+((-5)\cdot (76))+((7)\cdot (35-5k))\\ &=(48k+120)+(-380)+(245-35k)\\ &=13k-15\end{aligned}

$$
